header.status_line: Lineage is coded on Mark 16: 20 reception links, move-native, each typed by vehicle / function / fidelity / certainty AND carrying a SEAM (the unsaid in the borrowing) -- 20 of 20 project to a gap (reception on the unsaid). It is THE Connect seam, and the honest finding is that the seam is a FRONTIER: connect_edge holds 0 LINEAGE edges; lineage_record is the populated store of record.

what_it_is: Lineage codes what earlier text a move stands on -- the tributaries that flow into it -- and how it treats that source: by what vehicle (quotation / allusion / echo / paraphrase / structural), for what function (authorize / argue / problematize / scaffold / ornament / oppose), whether the borrowing is marked, and in which direction it shifts the source's sense (preserves / extends / repurposes / inverts). Crucially it also codes the SEAM: the unsaid IN the borrowing -- the relationship the citing text leaves implicit.
why_it_matters: Lineage is where reception becomes an object. A text that stands on Isaiah's suffering-servant WITHOUT saying so is making a claim in the negative space -- and that unsaid is exactly what the tradition later makes said. The seam (phrased interrogatively under the contested-echo guard) is that negative space held open honestly. Reception lands on BOTH the said (the citing move) and the unsaid (the gap the borrowing leaves), so Lineage is a primary site of the project's 'make the unsaid said'.

how_it_works.the_method_does: for each move that leans on an earlier source, records the upstream source_ref + the five typed enums + the seam (the unsaid), anchoring fidelity against the corpus where the upstream is itself coded (else flagging model-reconstructed + lowering confidence), and gating contested echoes (phrased interrogatively, interest capped).
how_it_works.you_get_back: a move-native set of reception links, each with its typed borrowing + its seam + a projection to the gap it reads.

pipeline_context.note: sibling terms glossed so the card stands alone.
pipeline_context.move: one small action a text makes (agent does an operation to something, with a result) -- the unit the pipeline codes; the grain Lineage attaches reception to.
pipeline_context.Decompose: the node that breaks a passage into moves; Lineage reads those moves to find what each one stands on.
pipeline_context.Situate: the parent node; Lineage is its 'what it stands on' aspect.
pipeline_context.Connect: the node that codes in-text + cross-text edges; its LINEAGE edge-KIND is meant to be Lineage's other view (currently empty -- see reconcile).
pipeline_context.the seam (the unsaid): sense 1: the UNSAID in a borrowing -- the relationship the citing text leaves implicit (stored in lineage_record.seam, projected to a gap). This is the reader-facing concept.
pipeline_context.the Connect seam (the join): sense 2 (distinct): the intended ARCHITECTURAL join between lineage_record and Connect's LINEAGE edges. The 'seam_reconcile' below is about THIS sense -- do not conflate it with the unsaid.
pipeline_context.reception-on-the-unsaid: a link that targets a GAP (a coded silence) rather than a move -- the tradition making an earlier silence said.
pipeline_context.the store of record: the ONE table a fact authoritatively lives in (s2.13); for Lineage that is lineage_record, not connect_edge.
pipeline_context.Tributary: the output Lineage feeds: the earlier sources flowing into a text, drawn as tributaries.
pipeline_context.the contested-echo guard: the null-guard: a low-certainty link is stored but GATED -- its seam is phrased as a QUESTION, not asserted, and its interest is capped.
pipeline_context.PI: the principal investigator (the researcher) -- who locks methodology calls like the a/b/c reconcile.

the_method_applied.note: Mark 16's reception links (a sample shown with their seam). Every link here targets a gap (reception on the unsaid); the seam is phrased interrogatively where the certainty is contested-echo.

worked_links.seam: Imports the white-robed heavenly-messenger figure of Danielic apocalyptic as the visual register for the tomb's interpreter, but leaves unsaid whether this 'young man' is an angel in Daniel's sense or something more ambiguous (a human interpreter, a narrative cipher).

Imports the standard seer-terror response to angelophany as the women's reaction, but leaves unsaid whether the women are being cast as prophetic seers or as failed ones who cannot receive the revelation.
Imports the angelic 'do not fear' formula that opens a revelatory speech, but leaves unsaid whether the command actually lands — since M26 says fear governs the women anyway.

Is MARK-16-WEB standing on Hosea 6:2 / Isaiah 26:19 here — and if so, what shifts? (Imports the prophetic 'raising on the third day / the dead shall live' register as the grammar for what has happened to Jesus, but leaves unsaid whether Hosea's collective national restoration is being individuated onto one person or preserved as corporate.)

worked_links.stands_on: tradition-register: Greco-Roman/Jewish empty-tomb + translation/vanishing scene (e.g. 2 Kings 2; Genesis 5:24)
worked_links.seam: Is MARK-16-WEB standing on tradition-register: Greco-Roman/Jewish empty-tomb + translation/vanishing scene (e.g. 2 Kings 2; Genesis 5:24) here — and if so, what shifts? (Participates in the conventional 'the body is not here — behold the place' scene of a translated/vanished figure, but leaves unsaid whether Jesus is being cast as an Elijah-type translation or as something categorically new (raised, not merely taken).)

Is MARK-16-WEB standing on Genesis 1:5 / Genesis 1:1-5 here — and if so, what shifts? (Imports the 'first day' + 'when the sun had risen' language as the register of a new creation-dawn, but leaves unsaid whether Mark is claiming the resurrection IS a new Genesis-beginning or only borrowing its light-at-dawn register.)

where_saved.plain: Reception links save to lineage_record (one row per citing move x upstream source), move-native, keyed on source_key. honest_limits: THE CONNECT SEAM IS A FRONTIER. connect_edge holds 0 LINEAGE edges; lineage_record holds the 20 Mark-16 links via a separate path. The plan's 'consumes Connect's LINEAGE edges' is inverted: lineage_record is the store of record. No green pill for a consumes-the-edges claim. See reconcile (answer: two stores).
The five enums are controlled-by-convention (CHECK-constrained but no formal vocab table + definitions doc the drawer reads live). Owed: a live vocab source, so they render live like Frame's.
6 of 20 Mark-16 links are contested-echo (the lowest certainty) -- stored but GATED: their seam is a question, not an assertion, and interest is capped. Honest, not hidden.

The nine typed fields (F1-F9) are: source_ref, borrowing_vehicle, markedness, borrowing_function, the seam, fidelity_direction, source_home/witness_version, link_certainty, reception_link. The drawer surfaces the five closed enums + the seam; the rest are provenance/anchoring fields.

research_view.decision_trail: CONTRACT_situate_closed_open_grain_s162 (Lineage enums) - connect_edge_vocab SITUATE_VIEW (the intended seam) - the S163 reconcile finding (two stores; lineage_record store of record).

seam_reconcile.question: Are lineage_record and connect_edge's LINEAGE edges ONE store (two views) or TWO stores?

evidence.lineage_record: 20 Mark-16 reception links; 9 typed fields (F1-F9) incl. fidelity_direction + the SEAM (the unsaid) + seam_gap_id -> source_move_gap; move-native. The POPULATED store of record.
evidence.connect_edge_LINEAGE: 0 rows. The intended Connect-side view (edge_types CITES, REUSES, BEQUEATHS, RE-READS, INHERITS-ACROSS) is EMPTY.
evidence.schema_gap: the two tables have DIFFERENT schemas: lineage_record is far richer (fidelity_direction, markedness, witness_version, the seam) than a connect_edge LINEAGE edge (edge_type + target_level + warrant). They OVERLAP in intent ('text stands on earlier text') but are not the same store.

seam_reconcile.consequence: The plan's 'Situate:Lineage CONSUMES Connect's LINEAGE edges' is INVERTED from reality: today lineage_record is the store of record and connect_edge LINEAGE is empty. Situate:Lineage consumes lineage_record; it does NOT re-code. No green pill for a consumes-the-edges claim.

options.a (recommended): KEEP lineage_record as the store of record; make the connect_edge LINEAGE view a DERIVED PROJECTION (a read of lineage_record, not a re-code). Lossless; preserves the reception schema + the seam/gap.
options.b: MIGRATE to connect_edge as the store -- move lineage_record's 9 fields + seam onto LINEAGE edges. A large schema merge that risks losing the reception-specific fields. Not recommended.
options.c: RETIRE the Connect-side LINEAGE-edge claim -- Connect POINTS to lineage_record instead of holding its own LINEAGE edges. Simplest; drops the 'two views' framing.

seam_reconcile.recommendation: (a). lineage_record is purpose-built for reception (markedness, fidelity_direction, witness_version, the seam/gap); a thin Connect edge cannot carry it without becoming lineage_record. Deriving the Connect view is cheap + lossless; the reverse is a lossy merge.
seam_reconcile.decision: LOCKED option (a) -- Decision 225 (PI, S163). lineage_record IS the store of record; Situate:Lineage renders from it (does not re-code). The Connect LINEAGE 'view', if wanted, is a DERIVED PROJECTION generated from lineage_record (tagged provenance='derived-from-lineage_record'), never a second authored store. The projection script is a small follow-up; the store-of-record lock stands without it.

run_and_record._this_is_the_agent_spec: everything needed to RUN this engine and record a result, in one block. The rest of the card is written for a human reader; nothing there is required to act.

black_box_contract.reads: see the engine script's header contract.
black_box_contract.writes: see the engine script's header contract.
black_box_contract.upstream: Decompose (source_move) must already have run for this key; Situate refines an existing moveset.
black_box_contract.gates: the run tag names one run, never a text; CHECK-constrained values are coerced against the vocab SSOT before write; an empty model response fails loud rather than writing a partial batch.

run_and_record.how_to_read_the_pills: a pill is the verdict of one DATED run, not a live status; where it and the card body disagree, the body is current. whats_next is generated fresh on every build.

before_you_run.decompose_first: Situate codes a text Decompose has already broken into moves, and the move-grain aspects read that moveset directly. Against an empty moveset a run does not error, it silently produces nothing. Check: SELECT COUNT(*), MAX(run_tag) FROM source_move WHERE source_key='<key>';
before_you_run.the_text_file: --text-file takes plain UTF-8. The reproducible way to make one is the LIBRARY checkout (shared_terms.text_checkout); a hand-pasted file works once but flag it in evidence_basis.
before_you_run.the_card_builder_is_mark_16_only: the CODERS run on any text; the drawer BUILDERS have the Mark 16 keys hardcoded and take no arguments. A new text can be coded and queried today, but its card cannot be generated, so its Cold Read cannot run. The parameterised builder is owed.

naming_conventions.run_tag: <textslug>_s<session>_<YYYYMMDD>, e.g. mark16_s170_20260813. One tag per RUN, not per text, so a re-code never overwrites an older run. Lands in: lineage_record.run_tag (a real column on this store). Older rows carry pre-convention tags (form_v1_s168, witness_s161, ood_s168) — historical, do not copy, and the reason a query must name its run.
naming_conventions.deployed_drawer_file: ../grammarofmeaning-site/engine/data/goldenpath/<text_slug>/lineage_node_drawer.json — the SIBLING deploy repo (what other cards call DEPLOY_REPO), not this one. text_slug is the source_key lowercased without punctuation: MARK-16-WEB -> mark16, MARK-16-GRC -> mark16_grc, TTC-CH1-EN -> ttc_ch1. A new text needs its directory made first (mkdir -p).
naming_conventions.cold_read_run_doc: pm/30_methodology/engine/COLDREAD_situate_lineage_run_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md — run_cold_read.py writes it and prints the path. Pass --date or the filename carries the wrong day.
naming_conventions.vs_wild_run_doc: pm/30_methodology/engine/VALIDATION_situate_lineage_vs_wild_run_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md — YOU write this one. The runner only drops the wild arm in field_ed/_persona_engine/out/situate_vs_wild/; the comparison against the instrument arm is yours to write, and seed_card_check.py fails loud if the cited file is absent.
naming_conventions.the_account_flag: --account hds picks which Claude Max plan the SDK call uses (Tier 1, $0). Check it is live first: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/lib/sdk_account_refresh.py hds --check

how_to_record_a_verdict.step_1: run the Cold Read: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/run_cold_read.py --node situate.lineage --drawer-file <the deployed drawer json for this text> --date <YYYY-MM-DD> --account hds  (it prints the COLDREAD run-doc path it wrote; see naming_conventions).
how_to_record_a_verdict.step_2: add ONE ROWS entry to scripts/analysis/seed_card_check.py of exactly this shape:

rows_entry_shape.run_doc: <the COLDREAD run-doc path run_cold_read.py just printed>

how_to_record_a_verdict.step_3: run ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/seed_card_check.py  (it FAILS LOUD unless the cited run_doc exists on disk); the verdict lands in card_check and renders as the pill. Seeding just means adding that ROWS entry and running the script: there is no other step.
how_to_record_a_verdict.the_bar: PASS = a fresh reader can RUN the engine from this card (Cold Read) and FIND where the prior work lives (Cold Start), with no broken gaps, honest limits flagged, and the card TIGHT — a reader should not be able to cut a third of it without loss. Not zero-clarifications: close the broken gaps, flag the limits, cut the padding, stop.

how_to_run_vs_wild.what_it_asks: does our scaffolding beat the same text read by an unscaffolded LLM given none of the instrument's fields. Primary metric is RELIABILITY (do repeated runs agree), not eloquence. Scope the wild arm to ONLY this aspect's job: an unscoped wild reader borrows the other layers' work and appears to win.
how_to_run_vs_wild.step_2_instrument_arm: this aspect's coded rows, already in its store. Comparison protocol: pm/30_methodology/engine/VALIDATION_situate_vs_wild_RUNSHEET_s170_2026-08-11.md.
how_to_run_vs_wild.step_3_record: record it like a Cold Read, with check_name 'vs_wild'.
how_to_run_vs_wild.for_a_new_text: PROMPTS in the runner is {aspect: prompt}; copy an entry and swap the text's name. It currently holds sitz / transmission / lineage, all written for Mark 16.
how_to_run_vs_wild.honest_limit: per §2.14 the DECISIVE run is on an UNDERSTUDIED text. On Mark 16 a naive model scores well from memory of the commentary, so parity there measures recall, not the instrument.

foundation_codes._what: the honesty tags on EVERY Situate coding, whatever wrote it. C4/R7 = evidence_basis + certainty (on what basis, how sure). C8/R3 = scope_level (at what grain). Grammar situate_foundation_v1, rendered from scripts/lib/situate_foundation_vocab.py.

evidence_basis (C4/R7).external-material: archaeology / epigraphy / material culture attests it.
evidence_basis (C4/R7).scholarly-consensus-with-citation: the field agrees AND a real citation is attached (corpus/DR only, never LLM memory).
evidence_basis (C4/R7).strongly-inferred: the coder reasoned it from strong, multi-source warrant (not from the coded text alone).
evidence_basis (C4/R7).internally-inferred: inferred FROM the text being coded — the context-laundering flag; downstream may EXCLUDE.
evidence_basis (C4/R7).LLM-proposed: a model proposed it with no external warrant (make the LLM-ness visible, §2.8).
evidence_basis (C4/R7).contested: the field actively disagrees; there is no settled basis.

certainty (C4/R7).low: the coder would not defend this value against a competing reading; treat as provisional.
certainty (C4/R7).med: the coder's best reading, but a competing reading is live (record it in alternative_hypothesis).
certainty (C4/R7).high: the coder would defend this value; no live competing reading at this grain.

scope_level (C8/R3).text: the whole source — the coding is a property of the work, not of any one part of it.
scope_level (C8/R3).pericope: the source's NATIVE sub-division (Mark 16:1-8 vs 16:9-20). Where no native division is marked, fall back to the Connect bundle / spine-segment — do NOT invent a new pericope primitive (R3).
scope_level (C8/R3).move: a single move (one operation plus its arguments), as produced by Decompose.

foundation_codes.alternative_hypothesis (C4/R7): OPEN free text: the competing reading the coder rejected. Expected whenever certainty is low or med.

codes_glossary.--moves-tag (in the run command): the run_tag of the Decompose moveset Lineage runs OVER, not a new tag. Find it with: SELECT DISTINCT run_tag FROM source_move WHERE source_key='<key>' AND run_tag LIKE 'move_grammar_v2%' ORDER BY run_tag DESC LIMIT 1. The --run-tag flag is the NEW tag for this lineage run.
codes_glossary.seam (disambiguation): TWO senses: (a) the F5 seam QUESTION a link raises; (b) a structural seam in the text. This card means (a) unless it says otherwise.

shared_terms.text_checkout: the LIBRARY's package of a text, and the mandated read path: verbatim (byte-identical to the stored passage text, hashed), anchored (carries {source_id, passage_id, verse_markers}), and versioned (a pinned snapshot). Engines code the checkout OFFLINE rather than reading the live DB, and results ingest back joined on the anchor. Build one with: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/build_checkout_package_s162.py --source-id <id> --ref "Mark 16" --out <path>  (optional: --verse-prefix / --section-prefix to pick the in-text markers, --edition WEB, --version v1). It resolves a source already in-corpus and chunked.
shared_terms.move: one operation plus its arguments: the derived sense-unit Decompose produces. Distinct from a passage, which is the source's own container (verse, pericope, paragraph).
shared_terms.wild: an unscaffolded LLM read of the same text, given none of the instrument's fields. The control arm.

methodology_tags.§2.1: code from the text's own terms; do not force a pre-set label (anti-pre-anchoring).
methodology_tags.§2.8: bias-visibility: name the conditions so corpus skew stays auditable, not hidden.
methodology_tags.§2.14: test the method out-of-domain (an understudied text), not only the one it was tuned on.
methodology_tags.§2.16: render from data: the card is generated from the coding, so it cannot silently drift.
methodology_tags.§2.13: single store of record: canonical data lives in a DB table (mirrored to Neon), not a loose file.
